Odin × Godot

Workflow: builds, editor tools, and debugging

12 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Odin scripts are AOT-compiledBuildingLive editing (show-on-save)Editor validation, autocomplete, and highlightingDebugging

This guide covers script builds, reloads, editor tools, and debugging. The scripts compile into native code, which determines how the editor updates properties and how you inspect a running game.

Odin scripts are AOT-compiled#

Your .odin scripts compile ahead of time into a native shared library (.dylib / .so / .dll) loaded through GDExtension. Godot executes the compiled procedures, so source changes require a build and library reload:

Capability Odin scripts Why
_ready / _process / signals / @export / methods ✅ Supported dispatched through a typed registry
Hot reload on save ✅ Recompile + swap (a few seconds) the library must be rebuilt before it can be loaded
eval / expression / a REPL ❌ Impossible nothing to evaluate source at runtime
In-editor breakpoints / step / pause / expression-eval in the debugger panel ❌ No the GDScript VM never sees your compiled proc — use lldb
New @export appearing instantly on save ⚠️ Needs a recompile the export lives in the compiled dll; the editor rebuilds for you (a moment's latency)
Editor remote scene tree / live property edit ✅ Yes engine-side, not script-line
lldb breakpoints, bt, memory inspection ✅ Supported a script dll is a native C library — debug it as one

Use the editor tools for builds and property inspection, and a native debugger for procedure-level execution.

Building#

In the editor, Project → Tools → Build Odin Scripts starts a background build of the project's scripts library and reports progress in the Output panel. Saving a script triggers the same build. Use the command line for CI, headless builds, or work from the source repository.

build/build_scripts.sh [PROJECT_DIR] [SCRIPTS_DIR] runs the full pipeline:

  1. builds the scriptgen preprocessor,
  2. runs it over the scripts dir to emit the *.gen.odin build artifacts beside your sources (you never edit these; the loader ignores them as attachable scripts). There are three kinds: odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin, one per package directory, holding the registration code for every script in that directory; odin_godot_boot.gen.odin, the init shim; and odin_godot_guard.gen.odin, the staleness guard, a compile-time #load_hash assert per authored source. A build path that skips this step (a bare odin build against yesterday's *.gen.odin) fails at compile time, naming the drifted file instead of silently compiling stale descriptors,
  3. builds the scripts dll (odin build <scriptsdir> -build-mode:dll with -custom-attribute:gd_method -custom-attribute:gd_connect -custom-attribute:gd_rpc -custom-attribute:gd_command -custom-attribute:gd_tick -custom-attribute:gd_input -custom-attribute:gd_sample -custom-attribute:gd_step -custom-attribute:gd_event -custom-attribute:gd_half -custom-attribute:gd_message, which let the Odin compiler accept the marker attributes), and
  4. builds the core dll.
Shell
nix develop --command bash -c 'bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/survivors'
# -> examples/survivors/bin/{libodinscripts.dylib, libodin_godot.dylib}

Defaults target tests/phase35; pass your project dir as the first argument. The repo root (for the godot collection) is derived from the script's own location, overridable with ODIN_GODOT_ROOT. If odin is not on PATH, pass it explicitly as ODIN=/abs/path/to/odin.

If the project has script modules (res://modules/<name>/), the same command also builds one libodinscripts_<name>.<ext> per module (BUILD_MODULES=0 opts out).

Live editing (show-on-save)#

Adding an Odin @export changes the compiled registration code. The property becomes available after the scripts library is rebuilt and reloaded. The editor runs that sequence when you save:

  1. On save, the editor starts a rebuild on a worker thread while the UI keeps processing. odin build takes a few seconds, and rapid saves coalesce into one rebuild. Running and exported games do not recompile themselves.
  2. After a successful build, the next editor frame swaps in the library, rebinds live instances, and refreshes Inspector property lists without an editor restart. State preservation depends on the layout and callback conditions listed below.

Format on save. When odinfmt is reachable (it ships with ols; also the odin_godot/odinfmt_bin setting), saving a script writes formatted code to disk and updates the open buffer in place. The change is a single undo step, the caret position is preserved, and no unsaved dot appears. A project-root odinfmt.json is honored. Sources that don't parse yet save unformatted (never blocked); disable with the odin_godot/format_on_save project setting.

A top-toolbar status badge shows Odin: building… during a rebuild and flashes green live ✓ (X.Xs) after a swap. A failed build leaves a red build FAILED badge; read the compiler errors in the Output panel. The badge hides when idle.

Pressing Play during a rebuild waits for it to finish. A failed build blocks launch and reports an error in Output so the game cannot run the previous library after a failed save. This uses EditorPlugin._build, the hook also used by C# to compile before launch.

In a project using script modules, the saved resource path identifies the module to rebuild. The worker skips unrelated module trees, and coalesced saves retain all affected roots. Saving under res://modules/enemies/ rebuilds that library while retaining the other modules' libraries, instances, and globals. The replaced library's own package globals reset. A slower background check catches external edits and deletions that did not trigger a save callback.

Saving under res://shared/ rebuilds every module because each can import that read-only shared tree. See Script Modules for details.

Finding the compiler. The editor often has no odin on its PATH (e.g. launched from the macOS app, not a shell). Point it at the binary with the odin_godot/odin_bin project setting, or set the ODIN environment variable, or launch the editor from the Nix shell. If none resolves, reload-on-save warns once and is skipped (the editor keeps working). The scripts package defaults to res://scripts; override with odin_godot/scripts_dir.

Manual trigger. If save detection misses (or you changed something outside the saved file), force the rebuild+reload+refresh by reloading the script, for example with load("res://scripts/your_script.odin").reload(true) from a tool script or the editor's script-reload affordance. This runs the exact same path as save.

Caveats.

  • Adding/removing/reordering struct fields changes the layout: exported values are preserved by name across the swap, but non-exported private fields reset (the same reload caveat GDScript has).
  • The live Inspector panel repaint after a swap is a visual editor behavior; the property list it reads is updated immediately in-process (verified headless), but eyeballing the panel repaint needs a display.
  • Native DLL generations are ownership-bounded. Ordinary live instances transfer to the new generation, and the old image unloads at the closed execution gate. A live instance whose class was removed keeps only its exact old generation until that instance is freed.
  • Procedure-bearing state (including nested events.Event and flow.Action containers) is detected recursively. Define <struct>_reload and rebuild that state there. Without the hook, the instance deliberately remains on its coherent old code and emits an actionable warning; intermediate generations still unload. Returned Inspector property lists hold a separate core-cache lease and never pin executable code.

Editor validation, autocomplete, and highlighting#

Validation, completion, and highlighting run in native editor builds. The web build stubs these tools. If a required binary is missing, the feature warns once and the editor continues running.

Live error squiggles (_validate)#

The editor displays Odin compiler errors as inline squiggles and Errors-panel entries. Syntax checking uses the compiler's parser in-process. A missing brace or incomplete expression is reported on the first debounce, and a buffer with syntax errors does not proceed to type checking. The recorded parser time is ~0.1 ms.

Type checking runs on the package because a single .odin file is not a compilation unit. The worker copies the package and its relative imports to a temporary overlay, replaces the edited file with the unsaved buffer, and runs odin check. It maps ‹file›(‹line›:‹col›) Error: ‹msg› diagnostics back to the editor. A result cache lets the editor return while the background check runs. Recorded first-call latency is ~0.03 ms; the warm package check is ~0.5 s on a game-sized package. Squiggles update on the next debounce after completion.

The godot collection root resolves in this order: odin_godot/root setting, ODIN_GODOT_ROOT environment variable, then the installed addon's location. A standard addons/odin_godot/ install needs no root override. Set odin_godot/root for a collection stored elsewhere.

_validate reports squiggles for the open file. If its edit causes an error in a sibling file, that error appears in Output during rebuild-on-save rather than as a live squiggle in the sibling.

Autocomplete (_complete_code, backed by ols)#

The ols Odin language server provides completions such as gd.node2d_set_p → node2d_set_position, with each symbol's type or signature beside its name. The editor retains one ols subprocess over stdio for the session. Recorded warm completion time is ~17–19 ms, compared with ~0.5–1.25 s for spawning and indexing on each request. If that process cannot start or exits, the editor falls back to a fresh spawn and then restarts the session. Select the binary with odin_godot/ols_bin, the OLS environment variable, or PATH. The Nix shell includes ols.

Syntax highlighting#

.odin files are token-colored in the Script panel (keywords, comments, strings, numbers, PascalCase types, proc calls). It's registered on the first editor frame and touches only the Script editor. Limitation: block comments are highlighted per-line, so a /* … */ spanning lines isn't tracked across them.

Icons#

A script class gets a custom icon via the //gd:icon <res-path> marker (shown in the Scene / FileSystem docks and Create-Node dialog, like a GDScript @icon). A script that sets no //gd:icon falls back to a bundled Odin mark (res://addons/odin_godot/icon.svg), so .odin scripts are recognizable rather than showing the generic script glyph. Override the default per project with the odin_godot/default_icon setting (point it at your own icon, or "" to use the engine generic). The default is existence-checked, so a non-standard install without the icon shows the generic one.

Find in Files#

The script editor's Find in Files (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F) searches .odin files. Godot's search file-type list is a hardcoded set (gd, cs, gdshader) with no hook for a GDExtension scripting language, so on load the Odin editor plugin appends odin to the editor/script/search_in_file_extensions project setting. The value is applied in-memory each session (your project.godot is left untouched), and the search dialog re-reads it every time it opens, so the *.odin filter checkbox is there and checked by default.

The Inspector does not provide documentation tooltips for @export fields or methods. Autocomplete shows type signatures as described above.

Generated files are hidden in the FileSystem dock#

The build writes one odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin registration file per scripts directory, plus the boot shim and staleness guard. Each must live in its package directory because Odin packages use one directory.

Generated files cannot be attached or opened as scripts in the editor. The plugin hides them from the FileSystem dock after each dock rebuild. Godot's filesystem scan selects by extension, so it still sees .gen.odin as .odin and provides no per-file exclusion hook. The files remain on disk and remain visible to external editors, git, and extension-based Find in Files.

To show them (e.g. when inspecting what scriptgen emits), set the odin_godot/show_generated_files project setting to true; it takes effect at the next dock rebuild (toggling a file save or reopening the project is enough).

Any *.gen.odin a build does not produce is deleted by the next one, printing scriptgen: removed stale <path> (not generated by this run). That covers a deleted script's leftovers and, on the first build after upgrading odin_godot, the older layout's per-source <name>.gen.odin files.

Editor settings reference#

Set these as project settings (they also have env fallbacks for shell-launched editors):

Setting Env fallback Purpose
odin_godot/odin_bin ODIN absolute path to the odin compiler (reload-on-save, validation)
odin_godot/ols_bin OLS absolute path to the ols language server (autocomplete)
odin_godot/emcc_bin EMCC absolute path to Emscripten's emcc (web export only)
odin_godot/root ODIN_GODOT_ROOT the odin_godot checkout, for the -collection:godot root
odin_godot/scripts_dir — the scripts package (default res://scripts)
odin_godot/export_optimization ODIN_EXPORT_OPT Odin -o: level for exported builds: none/minimal/size/speed/aggressive (default speed)
odin_godot/default_icon — editor icon for .odin scripts with no //gd:icon (default res://addons/odin_godot/icon.svg; "" = engine generic)
odin_godot/show_generated_files — true shows *.gen.odin build artifacts in the FileSystem dock (hidden by default)

Dev builds vs. exports. The editor's rebuild-on-save loop compiles at -o:none so saves stay fast. Exports (desktop and web) compile at odin_godot/export_optimization (default speed) so shipped games are optimized. The two are independent. To remove bounds checks and assertions, append -no-bounds-check -disable-assert through SCRIPT_BUILD_FLAGS when running the export build script directly.

Debugging#

Use logging, lldb, and native crash backtraces to debug the scripts library. Debugging contains the full reference and verified transcripts. The main entry points are below.

Logging: gd.print / gd.error / gd.warn#

Odin
import gd "godot:godot"

gd.print("player ready")        // -> stdout + the editor Output panel
gd.print_int(score)             // i64 (also print_float / print_bool / print_value)
gd.warn("coin value was 0")     // yellow, non-fatal (push_warning)
gd.error("Hud node missing")    // RED in Output/Debugger, with context (push_error)

The logging helpers are contextless and do not import core:fmt, avoiding that dependency in the wasm build. For formatted output, use Odin's fmt before calling them:

Odin
import "core:fmt"
gd.print(fmt.ctprintf("score=%d", score))   // ctprintf -> temp cstring, what gd.print wants
gd.print_str(fmt.tprintf("hp=%d/%d", hp, max_hp))

Native debugging with lldb#

Project > Tools > Debug Game (LLDB) opens a terminal running the game under lldb. Debug Game (Break at Cursor) sets a breakpoint on the script line at the caret. Generate VS Code Debug Config configures VS Code/CodeLLDB for F5 launch and clickable breakpoints in .odin files. The shell launcher uses the same setup, including macOS SIP re-signing and handling lldb's :: parsing issue:

Shell
build/debug_game.sh --break player.odin:51 tests/showcase

The dlls carry full DWARF (-debug -use-single-module): file:line breakpoints, stepping, and frame variable with typed args. frame variable *self prints the live script struct, and the auto-loaded godot_lldb.py summaries render godot.String/String_Name/ Variant values. A script panic freezes the session at the panic site. See debugging.md for the full tour.

Other editors and IDEs#

Project > Tools > Generate ols.json (IDE Completion) writes an ols.json at the project root: ols-based editors (Neovim, Zed, Sublime, Helix) get completion for your scripts + the godot collection immediately, and JetBrains IDEs import it via the Odin Support plugin (right-click the file). Rider supports editing but cannot debug native code with the plugin on Rider ≥ 2025.2. CLion/IDEA Ultimate can, pointed at the debuggable Godot copy. See debugging.md for details.

Crashes and panics are reported automatically#

A crash or panic in script code is reported: an Odin panic/assert pushes a red ODIN_SCRIPT_PANIC <message> (file:line) error to the editor Output, and a raw fatal signal (SIGSEGV etc., e.g. an engine call on a nil handle, on macOS/Linux) prints an ODIN_GODOT_CRASH report to stderr with the faulting Odin proc symbolized, pushes a one-line error toward the editor, and still chains to Godot's own crash handler. See the "What you see when the game crashes" section of Debugging.

To inspect the fault, run the crashing scenario under lldb and use bt, or read the native backtrace printed to stderr (grep it for your package name). On macOS the same backtrace is in the .ips report under ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/.

A _debug_get_current_stack_info virtual is wired and produces a correct native Odin backtrace when invoked, but Godot only calls it during an active remote-debug session, so it does not automatically surface a script-line stack on a plain error. Use lldb for your day-to-day stack view. See Debugging for the full account.

Web / wasm#

In the browser there's no dlopen, no native stack, and no lldb. Debug with logging (gd.print → the JS console) and browser devtools. See Exporting.
